# Gridgeist

Use grid, type, spacing, rules, and real product content as the visual language;
decoration supports the system.

## Workflow

1. Inspect content, audience, routes, behavior, tokens, components, and rendered
   desktop/mobile UI. Preserve intentional brand and functionality.
2. State one thesis, such as “a precise learning workspace built on an editorial
   grid, quiet rules, dense evidence, and one blue accent.”
3. Define container, columns, spacing rhythm, type roles, colors, borders,
   radius, shadows, and responsive transformations as reusable tokens.
4. Compose hierarchy before detail. Align related content, vary section rhythm,
   and give one area clear dominance.
5. Implement semantic, keyboard-accessible behavior. Recompose mobile layouts
   instead of shrinking desktop.
6. Render and review in this order: clarity, hierarchy, alignment, typography,
   interaction/responsiveness, accessibility, implementation quality.

## Guardrails

- Use one coherent system and product-specific copy/evidence.
- Give borders, radius, shadows, color, and motion defined roles.
- Treat repeated cards, centered heroes, gradient blobs, excessive pills, and
  arbitrary icon boxes as diagnostic signals—not automatic prohibitions.
- Do not mistake empty space for hierarchy or outline every element with rules.
- Extract principles from references; do not copy another brand literally.

Record an approved direction in the active OpenSpec design when it affects the
shared product language. Verify the rendered result at representative desktop
and mobile widths.

References: read `references/design-language.md` to select influences and
`review-checklist.md` for the final rendered review.
